name: _grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback_backward
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::_grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback_backward(Tensor grad_output, Tensor input, Tensor grid, int interpolation_mode, int padding_mode, bool align_corners) -> (Tensor, Tensor). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for all registered overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must not be narrowed to this signature. Registered schemas supplied for this operator (all listed verbatim): aten::_grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback_backward(Tensor grad_output, Tensor input, Tensor grid, int interpolation_mode, int padding_mode, bool align_corners) -> (Tensor, Tensor). Semantics: backward of the 2D CPU fallback grid sampler. Given grad_output of shape (N, C, out_H, out_W), input of shape (N, C, H, W) and normalized grid of shape (N, out_H, out_W, 2), it returns the gradient with respect to input (same shape as input) and the gradient with respect to grid (same shape as grid). interpolation_mode selects bilinear (0), nearest (1) or bicubic (2); padding_mode selects zeros (0), border (1) or reflection (2); align_corners is a required bool. Measured native contract from the tests: `.default` is the only overload and it is a CompositeImplicitAutograd whose kernel is CPU-only, so operands are built on CPU rather than on flag_gems.device and float32 is the only accepted dtype; input and grid must both be rank-4 with matching batch size and grid last dimension of 2, otherwise ATen raises RuntimeError. interpolation_mode and padding_mode values are not validated by the kernel, so the valid enum is swept rather than tested as a negative case. The pytest also owns the autograd comparison, where the candidate's requires_grad is compared against the native reference's rather than asserted to an absolute value, and the error surface; this model expresses neither of those. The logical output count is two, matching the two ATen returns; each returned Tensor is one logical output and list-valued returns are not involved.
